data.content_ref: inline:The target's causal mechanism rests on a TSP-to-sorting-network analogy, but the disanalogies it itself enumerates undercut the mechanism without a bridging account. Simulated annealing requires a graded energy function so that the cooling schedule can accept 'worse' solutions with nonzero probability that decreases over time. The 0-1 principle yields a binary pass/fail signal — a candidate network either sorts all 8192 binary vectors or it does not — so a rewired or comparator-stripped network almost certainly fails the check, producing a flat (zero-gradient) landscape with no informative signal to guide the annealing walk. The target lists 'TSP solutions form a continuous distance landscape, while sorting networks have a discrete validation landscape' as a disanalogy but never specifies the energy function that would make SA operational on this discrete, all-or-nothing validation. Without such a function, the claim that SA will 'reliably find 45-comparator networks' lacks a causal mechanism: the shared structure of 'accept worse solutions temporarily' cannot function when there is no graded notion of 'worse' to accept.
